title: How Quantum Suicide Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain quantum suicide, a thought experiment devised by Max Tegmark to illustrate the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics. They cover quarks and photons, the observer effect and Heisenberg's uncertainty principle (with a blind-man-and-ball analogy), Hugh Everett's many-worlds theory and decoherence, the Copenhagen interpretation of Niels Bohr with superposition and wave function collapse, and Schrödinger's cat. The episode ends with listener mail about Hippie Rob's origin and a Kiva wedding jar fundraiser.

segments.title: Opening banter and quarks
segments.summary: Hosts joke about names and introduce quantum physics, quarks as building blocks of matter, and the Large Hadron Collider.

segments.title: Quantum suicide thought experiment
segments.summary: Josh explains Max Tegmark's quantum suicide thought experiment: a gun wired to a measured cork spin, and why the man would only perceive surviving clicks under the many-worlds view.

segments.title: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle and the observer effect
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss how observation affects quantum particles, using a blind person throwing a ball at a chair and photons moving a nano motor as analogies.

segments.title: Many-worlds interpretation and decoherence
segments.summary: Hugh Everett's many-worlds theory is described: each outcome splits the universe, with decoherence, and the hosts discuss how quantum suicide is used to support it.

segments.title: Copenhagen interpretation, superposition and Schrödinger's cat
segments.summary: The Copenhagen interpretation of Niels Bohr is covered, including superposition and wave function, along with Schrödinger's cat thought experiment and the rivalry with Heisenberg.

segments.title: Closing reflections on quantum theory
segments.summary: Hosts reflect on Bohr's quote that anyone not shocked by quantum theory has not understood it, and the many contradictory interpretations, then briefly discuss the Inception movie.

segments.title: Listener mail: Hippie Rob and Kiva wedding
segments.summary: A listener confirms Hippie Rob's first appearance in the How Stuff Works squatting episode, and Janna from Minnesota describes a wedding jar fundraiser that donated to Kiva loans for the show's team.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing reminder to send listener mail and promotional sign-off.
